subject: Slow down due to many persistent observers

messages.author: b39b358ba11a07d3
messages.subject: Slow down due to many persistent observers
parts:
Dear community and Joe,

I have a big and complex Shiny app (over 2000 lines) that does awesome things (automatically / with an interface process many GEO micro array data sets). Basically it does a bunch of processing, then provides an interactive UI for the user to modify and verify some things, then does more processing. It works, which is awesome.

The problem is that when getting user feedback on many data sets one after the other, it eventually slows down to be unusable. I have to the best of my ability traced this to the dynamic creation of buttons (required) and paired observers, that seem to persist, resulting in hundreds of observers, and I can't find a way to get rid of them.

I guess there are two solutions I can think of, but are outside of my knowledge of Shiny and outside of my googling abilities:
1) Assign some kind of consistent ID to the observers so that they over write themselves, or confine them to a list or reactive values. I tried this but I still couldn't overwrite them. Is it to do with R making copies of objects instead of passing a reference?
2) GO in and destroy the old observers. Again I tried this by assigning the observers to a list and then lapply .... destroy on that list and it didn't seem to have any effect.

Please help.

Thank you.

Djordje

Below is a minimal example:

##############################################################
##############################################################

library(shiny)
library(DT)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
 
  ## make a toy data frame
  DF <- data.frame(A = c(1,2), B = c(3,4), row.names = c("one","two"))
  ## make a DT output for it
  output$testData <- DT::renderDataTable(DF, selection = "single")
 
  output$message <- renderText("This minimal example illustrates issues with persistent observers building up over time. Every time you swap between the selected rows of the table, new observers are created that monitor the dynamically created action buttons. Each time a button observer is invalidated it will write a message to the console. The more times you swap between selected rows, the more persistent observers are created and the more console messages you get per click. I want to remove the previously created observers when changing the selected row. ")
 
  # get the last clicked row
  selectedRow <- reactive({
    req(input$testData_row_last_clicked)
    input$testData_row_last_clicked
  })
 
  # tell us which row it was
  output$selectedRow <- renderText(selectedRow())
 
 
  output$lastClick <- renderUI({
   
    req(selectedRow())
   
    list(
      lastclick =  renderText(selectedRow()),
      buttons = lapply(1:DF[selectedRow(),"A"], function(X){
        actionButton(paste0("go_", selectedRow(), X), "CLICK ME")
      })
    )
   
   
   
  })
 
# overarching observer for dynamic creation
  obs <- observe({
   
# make an observer for each input button that is current visible
    lapply(names(input)[grepl(paste0("go_", selectedRow()), names(input))], function(x) {
# print a message to the console
      print(paste0("Made observer for :", x))
      obsr <- observeEvent(
        {input[[x]]},{
          print(paste0("BUTTON ",x," WAS CLICKED"))
        }, ignoreNULL = TRUE, autoDestroy = TRUE)
     })
  })
 
# this is where I want to ideally clear previous observers
  obss <- observeEvent(
    {selectedRow()},{
      print("Somehow I want to clear previous observers here")
    }, ignoreNULL = TRUE, autoDestroy = TRUE)
 
 
 
}


########################################################################
# User Interface
########################################################################

ui <- fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    textOutput("message"),
    dataTableOutput("testData"),
    uiOutput("lastClick")
  )
)

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.subject: Re: Slow down due to many persistent observers
parts:
Thanks Joe,

I made it work with your tip. My problem was that my overarching observer was firing multiple times and creating a bunch more observers each time, so even though I was actually destroying the latest bunch, I didn't realize because the total number was still increasing.

Thanks a lot, and for Shiny. I'm a fan.

Cheers,

Djordje

messages.subject: Re: Slow down due to many persistent observers
parts:
Hi Joe and devs,

It turns out the slow down was not only due to persistent observers, as the problem has not gone away by destroying them - my app still becomes unusably slow as more interfaces are generated (it's fine for the first one).

Another sign I found was a build up of the data table related inputs in names(input). I reproduced the issue in the following minimal example:

#####################################################################

library(shiny)
library(DT)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
 
  ## make a toy data frame
  DF <- data.frame(A = c(1,2), B = c(3,4), row.names = c("one","two"))
  ## make a DT output for it
  output$testData <- DT::renderDataTable(DF, selection = "single")

output$message <- renderText("This minimal example illustrates issues with persistent inputs building up over time. Every time you swap between the selected rows of the table, new inputs are created for the data frames. The more times you swap between selected rows, the more persistent inputs are created. Can this be related to memory usage or something else that is slowing down my apps? ")

# get the last clicked row
  selectedRow <- reactive({
    req(input$testData_row_last_clicked)
    input$testData_row_last_clicked
  })
 
  # tell us which row it was
  output$selectedRow <- renderText(selectedRow())
 
 
  output$lastClick <- renderUI({
   
    req(selectedRow())
   
    list(
      lastclick =  renderText(selectedRow()),
      buttons = lapply(1:DF[selectedRow(),"A"], function(X){
        actionButton(paste0("go_", selectedRow(), X), "CLICK ME")

}),
      datas = lapply(1:DF[selectedRow(),"A"], function(X){renderDataTable(DF[selectedRow(),]) }),
      message1 = h3(renderText(paste0("length(names(input)): ", length(names(input))))),
      message2 = h3(renderText("names(input):")),
      inputnames = renderText(names(input))
    )
   
   
   
  })
 
  observer.list <- list()
 
  obs <- observe({
   
    observer.list <<- lapply(names(input)[grepl(paste0("go_", selectedRow()), names(input))], function(x) {

print(paste0("Made observer for :", x))
      obsr <- observeEvent(
        {input[[x]]},{
          print(paste0("BUTTON ",x," WAS CLICKED"))
        }, ignoreNULL = TRUE, autoDestroy = TRUE)
     })
  })

obss <- observeEvent(
    {selectedRow()},{

print("clear previously made observers")
      lapply(observer.list, function(X){ X$destroy() })
    }, ignoreNULL = TRUE, autoDestroy = TRUE, priority = 1)

}


########################################################################
# User Interface
########################################################################

ui <- fluidPage(
  mainPanel(
    textOutput("message"),
    dataTableOutput("testData"),
    uiOutput("lastClick")
  )
)

shinyApp(ui, server)

#####################################################################

As you can see from this example the number of inputs keeps increasing as you dynamically render more interfaces.

In my app I render a lot of data tables like this dynamically (2-20 per data set, 1 or more times per data set, hundreds of data sets), so this number builds up very quickly.

Could there be something I am missing here that is slowing my app down as it progresses? I do also see a constant rise in memory usage that is not intuitive. Can I remove these 'old' inputs, and will it help?

Thanks a lot.

Djordje
